text: Physics is the branch of science which deals with the study of matter, energy and their interactions. Physics falls under natural science, which is divided into three main branches: physics, chemistry and biology.

text: Density = mass / volume. In symbols, rho = m / V, where m is mass and V is volume. The density in Example 4.1 is expressed in kg/m^3. Example 4.1: A glass block has dimensions 0.12 m by 0.04 m by 0.10 m and mass 1.2 kg. Volume = 0.12 * 0.04 * 0.10 = 0.00048 m^3. Density = 1.2 / 0.00048 = 2500 kg/m^3.
transcription_style: source-verified excerpt with linearized mathematical notation

text: Relative density, R.D., is the ratio of the density of a substance to the density of water. R.D. = density of substance / density of water = mass of substance / mass of an equal volume of water. Relative density has no unit because it is the ratio of the same quantity. It is also known as specific gravity. A substance is denser than water if its relative density is greater than 1, and less dense than water if it is less than 1. Example 4.6: An object has density 7 g/cm^3. R.D. = (7 g/cm^3) / (1 g/cm^3) = 7.
transcription_style: source-verified excerpt with linearized mathematical notation

text: Upthrust is equal to the weight of the displaced fluid. This observation verifies Archimedes principle, which applies to objects of all densities. Upthrust depends on the weight of the fluid displaced.
transcription_style: source-verified excerpt with linearized mathematical notation

text: Hooke's law states that provided the elastic limit is not exceeded, the extension is directly proportional to the force applied. In the elastic region, the ratio of applied force F to the distance stretched e is the elastic force constant k. Thus, k = F / e. The SI unit of k is N/m. The elastic limit is the maximum point beyond which the material cannot return to its original shape when the deforming force is removed.
transcription_style: source-verified excerpt with linearized mathematical notation

topic: Pressure definition formula and SI unit
text: Pressure is the force acting normally or perpendicularly on a unit surface area of an object. Pressure P = normal force F / area A, or P = F / A. For a given force, a smaller area of application produces a larger pressure. The SI unit of pressure is the pascal, Pa. One pascal is one newton per square metre: 1 Pa = 1 N/m^2.
transcription_style: source-verified excerpt with linearized mathematical notation

text: Pressure in a liquid = height of the liquid column * density of the liquid * acceleration due to gravity. In symbols, P = h * rho * g. Pressure at a point in a liquid at rest depends on the depth and the density of the liquid. It does not depend on the area of the container. Pressure in a liquid increases with depth and acts equally in all directions.
transcription_style: source-verified excerpt with linearized mathematical notation

text: Speed is the rate of change in distance. Average speed is the rate at which an object travels. Speed v = distance s / time t, or v = s / t. Velocity is the rate of change of displacement. Velocity specifies a direction. If a car moves at constant speed around a bend, its direction changes continuously, so its velocity changes even when its speed remains constant. Example 8.1: Halima runs twice around a track of length 500 m. Distance covered = 500 * 2 = 1000 m. She ends at the starting point, so her displacement is 0 m.
transcription_style: source-verified excerpt with linearized mathematical notation

text: Acceleration describes the rate at which an object changes its velocity. Acceleration can result from a change in speed, direction, or both. Acceleration a = change in velocity / time taken = (v - u) / t. Here u is the initial velocity and v is the final velocity. The SI unit of acceleration is metre per second squared, written m/s^2.
transcription_style: source-verified excerpt with linearized mathematical notation

topic: Equations of uniformly accelerated linear motion
text: For linear motion with uniform acceleration, the first equation is v = u + a*t. The second equation is s = u*t + (1/2)*a*t^2. The third equation is v^2 = u^2 + 2*a*s. Here u is initial velocity, v is final velocity, a is acceleration, t is time and s is displacement. For uniform acceleration, average velocity = (u + v) / 2. The superscript ^2 means squared. These equations apply when acceleration is uniform.
transcription_style: source-verified excerpt with linearized mathematical notation

text: Work is done when a force acts on a body and the body moves in the direction of the applied force. Work done W = force F * distance d moved in the direction of the force, or W = F*d. The SI unit of work is joule, J, equivalent to newton metre. One joule is the work done when a force of one newton moves an object one metre in the direction of the force.
transcription_style: source-verified excerpt with linearized mathematical notation

text: Kinetic energy is energy possessed by an object due to its motion. The kinetic energy depends on mass and speed. For a body of mass m moving at speed v, KE = (1/2)*m*v^2. The SI unit of kinetic energy is joule, J, equivalent to kg*m^2/s^2. Change in kinetic energy = final kinetic energy - initial kinetic energy.
transcription_style: source-verified excerpt with linearized mathematical notation

topic: Gravitational potential energy formula and example
text: Gravitational potential energy depends on mass, acceleration due to gravity and height above a reference level. When the reference level is taken as zero potential energy, PE = m*g*h, where h is height above that reference level. Change in potential energy is equal to the work done in lifting the object. The SI unit of potential energy is joule. Example 9.5: A stone has mass 2 kg and is at height 25 m above the ground, with g = 10 m/s^2. PE = 2 * 10 * 25 = 500 J.
transcription_style: source-verified excerpt with linearized mathematical notation

text: Power is the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred. Power P = work done W / time t, or P = W / t. Power is measured in joules per second or watts. One watt is one joule per second: 1 W = 1 J/s. One kilowatt is 1000 W, one megawatt is 1000000 W, and one horsepower is 746 W.
transcription_style: source-verified excerpt with linearized mathematical notation
